comments.body:
Review remediation (2026-08-21) — narration moved out of the description to keep it under the
plan-review admission limit. What was factually wrong in the original plan and what was corrected,
with file:line evidence.

1. Vacuous acceptance criterion. The prior AC#1 grepped for "maximum context length". That phrase
   appears in NEITHER owner file — its only hit under `src/rebar` is
   `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py:78`. The criterion therefore passed on unmodified
   `main` and would still have named that file after a correct implementation. It now greps for
   "too many tokens", which is in the owned tuple.

2. A THIRD, deliberately different classifier exists. `workflow/completion_failures.py:46-79`
   `_is_token_exhaustion` omits the bare "context" substring the other two classifiers carry
   ("without mistaking generic context text") and additionally keys off a normalized `finish_reason`
   set (`:52-60`). A naive hint-string uniqueness guard would demand deleting it; folding it in
   would make any message containing the word "context" read as token exhaustion. It is now exempted
   by name and asserted unchanged.

3. The exit-code mapping was already centralised. `_cli/_llm_commands.py:45` (`_llm_error_exit_code`)
   and `:64-100` (`_disposition_exit_code`) are the two shared helpers; they are called by three
   verbs (`:147`, `:157`, `:231`, `:336`) plus `_commands/claim.py:120-123` and
   `_commands/composer.py:778-781`. There were never four hand-rolled copies, so there was nothing
   left to collapse.

4. Two verbs opt out of that mapping ON PURPOSE, and a shared mapping would silently change both:
   `scan-spec` returns a flat exit 1 on `LLMError` (`_llm_commands.py:188-190`), and its MCP twin
   `_mcp_llm.py:109-133` has no `except` at all; `verify-completion` (`_llm_commands.py:244-246`)
   carries the `verdict_obtainable is False → 11` rule from bug 2a6f and has no INDETERMINATE→2 arm.

5. The proposed `exit_code_for(outcome_or_coverage)` signature was structurally impossible.
   `_disposition_exit_code` reads `result["verdict"]` (accepting both the plan-review string form
   and the nested code-review dict) and calls `plan_review.resign.classify_plan_review_attestation`.
   Neither is reachable from an `LLMOutcome` nor from a `coverage` dict.

6. The `structured.py` merge is harmful and was already decided against.
   `structured._BAD_STOP_REASONS` (`structured.py:616-627`) is keyed by finish/stop reason
   (refusal / max_tokens / length / content_filter / error) and its values are the EXCEPTION text
   raised at `structured.py:646,648,676`. `failure.message_for` (`failure.py:355`) is keyed by the
   disjoint 8-member `ResolutionClass` vocabulary and returns operator remedy prose. The key spaces
   share no member, so `message_for("refusal")` evaluates to `None` and `check_stop_reason` would
   raise with no message at all. Bug `injurious-definable-badger` (closed, landed `0e41876787` via
   Gerrit 1525) already recorded the decision: "Leave `check_response`'s raise text unchanged
   (already accurate)."

7. The seam bug 2a6f/injurious-definable-badger hid in is already closed: one caller composed
   `message_for(...)` without the `finish_reason`; all three render sites now thread it
   (`_llm_commands.py:53-57,74-78` and `close_precheck.py:700-705`).

8. `close_precheck.py:691-714` diverges deliberately too — it additionally calls
   `failure.log_degrade` and `failure.close_gate_remedy`, and embeds the message in a `CommandError`
   rather than writing `llm-degrade: …` to stderr as the CLI helpers do.

Net effect: the story reduces to ONE genuine duplication — the eight-phrase `_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS`
tuple byte-identical in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:148-157` and
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:316-329` — plus its uniqueness guard. The other three proposed
consolidations are WITHDRAWN, not deferred.

comments.body:
Implementation pushed as Gerrit change 2074 (Change-Id If74eaa404c261ae0049633844b40482c866a0bef).

Verification of the plan's claims against the tree before review (all confirmed):
- The duplication is real and byte-identical: failure.py:148-157 vs sizing.py:316-329.
- AC greps run clean on the pre-change tree and discriminate: 'too many tokens' hit exactly
  {failure.py, sizing.py}; 'maximum context length' hit ONLY completion_failures.py:78 (the
  vacuous-AC finding is confirmed, and the corrected AC no longer has that defect).
- orchestrator.py:72 does bind _is_context_limit_error = sizing.is_context_limit_error at import
  time, and test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:45 monkeypatches the name as a string, so
  the def had to survive in sizing.
- Bug injurious-definable-badger's description does say 'Leave check_response's raise text
  unchanged (already accurate)', confirming the structured.py merge was decided against.
- No import cycle: failure.py imports only rebar.llm.errors.

file_impact was corrected from the withdrawn seven-file list to the three files actually touched;
that was also why the prior attestation kept going stale on unrelated _cli/_commands churn.
Title changed to match the delivered scope (the E3 advisory); title is not review material, so
the PASS attestation stayed certified.

Mutation evidence for the new tests (each perturbation restored afterwards):
- restore sizing's local tuple -> the uniqueness guard AND the live-read behaviour test go RED
  (this was the initial RED run);
- drop 'prompt is too long' from the owner tuple -> uniqueness guard + the verdict table go RED;
- scanner subset check -> intersection -> the partial-copy test goes RED;
- scanner never appends a hit -> three tests go RED;
- scanner ignores the escape marker -> the escape-marker test goes RED;
- match phrases as file substrings instead of AST string literals -> the prose test goes RED;
- drop the \S that makes the opt-out reason mandatory -> the escape-marker test goes RED;
- orchestrator stops aliasing the predicate -> the patchable-predicate test goes RED.
An earlier form of the reason rule survived mutation because two redundant checks masked each
other; the rule was single-sourced into the regex so the mutation now bites.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
LLM failure classification is duplicated in exactly ONE place: the context-length phrase list is
byte-identical in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:148-157` and
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:316-329`; `failure.py:144-147` records why ("kept local so this
low-level boundary module has no dependency on the plan_review package — the two must stay in
sync"). A fix to one silently leaves the other stale — the instalment pattern the review found.

## Approach
**Scope reduction — read this first.** The genuine content is ONE duplication: the eight-phrase
`_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS` tuple copied byte-for-byte into `sizing.py`. The other three consolidations the
original plan proposed are WITHDRAWN, not deferred: the retryable→exit-code mapping is ALREADY
centralised in `_cli/_llm_commands.py:45` (`_llm_error_exit_code`) and `:64-100`
(`_disposition_exit_code`), called by three verbs (`:147`, `:157`, `:231`, `:336`) plus
`_commands/claim.py:120-123` and `_commands/composer.py:778-781`, so there is no fourth hand-rolled
copy; the `structured.py` message merge is harmful and was decided against in a closed, merged bug
(see Deliberate divergences); and the MCP payload helper composes no exit code at all.
What remains is a one-line import change plus its guard.

`sizing.is_context_limit_error` stops carrying its own tuple and reads `failure._CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS`
instead. The `def is_context_limit_error` MUST STAY in `sizing.py` — `orchestrator.py:72` binds
`_is_context_limit_error = sizing.is_context_limit_error` at import time and
`test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:45` monkeypatches the name as a string, so a re-export
in its place would desynchronise both. The direction `sizing → failure` introduces no cycle
(`failure.py` imports only `rebar.llm.errors`; `sizing.py:26-32` already imports `rebar.llm.config`,
`.errors`, `.model_classes`, `.runner`) and preserves the boundary constraint `failure.py:144`
records.

Guard: the eight-phrase CONJUNCTION appears in exactly one file. Match the co-occurrence of all
eight literals within a single expression (per the epic's rule 2 — never a single common token such
as `"context"`), exempt the owner `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, honour a `# context-hints-ok: <reason>`
line marker.

### Deliberate divergences this story must NOT collapse
- `workflow/completion_failures.py:46-79` `_is_token_exhaustion` is a THIRD, intentionally different
  classifier: it omits the bare `"context"` substring the other two carry ("without mistaking
  generic context text") and keys off a normalized `finish_reason` set (`:52-60`). Folding it in
  would make any message containing the word "context" read as token exhaustion.
- `structured._BAD_STOP_REASONS` (`structured.py:616-627`) is NOT a copy of `failure.message_for`
  (`failure.py:355`): it is keyed by finish/stop reason (`refusal`/`max_tokens`/`length`/
  `content_filter`/`error`) with EXCEPTION text as values (raised at `structured.py:646,648,676`),
  while `message_for` is keyed by the disjoint 8-member `ResolutionClass` vocabulary and returns
  operator remedy prose. The key spaces share no member, so `message_for("refusal")` is `None` and
  `check_stop_reason` would raise with no message. Bug `injurious-definable-badger` (closed, landed
  `0e41876787` via Gerrit 1525) decided this: "Leave `check_response`'s raise text unchanged."
- `_llm_commands.py:188-190` (`scan-spec`) returns a flat exit **1** on `LLMError`; its MCP twin
  `_mcp_llm.py:109-133` has no `except` at all. Neither joins the disposition mapping.
- `_llm_commands.py:244-246` (`verify-completion`) carries an extra rule from bug 2a6f
  (`verdict_obtainable is False → 11`) and no INDETERMINATE→2 arm.
- `close_precheck.py:691-714` additionally calls `failure.log_degrade` and
  `failure.close_gate_remedy`, and embeds the message in a `CommandError` instead of writing
  `llm-degrade: …` to stderr as the CLI helpers do.
- `_disposition_exit_code` reads `result["verdict"]` (both the plan-review string and the nested
  code-review dict) and calls `plan_review.resign.classify_plan_review_attestation`; neither is
  reachable from an `LLMOutcome` or a `coverage` dict, so no `exit_code_for(...)` can replace it.

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` (drop the local tuple, import the owner's);
`src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (comment update only — the tuple is already correct);
`tests/unit/test_context_hints_single_source.py` (new; flat, as `tests/unit/llm/` does not exist).

Explicitly OUT of scope, for the reasons above: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`,
`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py`.

## Testing
Guard: the conjunction resolves to one file under `src/rebar` with the owner exempt, and is proven
to FLAG by reintroducing a second copy in a temp fixture, not just to pass. Namesakes it must
leave untouched: `run_failure.py:190-191`, `enrich.py:47` (docstrings quoting the phrases as prose),
`completion_failures.py:56,59,73`.

Pinning — must pass with no assertion edits, all under `tests/unit/`:
`test_llm_failure_classifier.py` (`:188-211`, both classifiers agree on a wrapped context error,
disagree on a refusal);
`test_change_input_not_an_outage_43d4.py::test_the_new_prefix_does_not_itself_look_like_a_context_limit`
(`:245-266`, the sharpest guard on this tuple);
`test_plan_review.py::test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (`:1331`, reaches the predicate via
the import-time alias `orchestrator._is_context_limit_error`);
`test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py` (`:45`, monkeypatches `sizing.is_context_limit_error`
by string — the `def` must survive); `test_llm_failure_matrix.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The eight-phrase list has exactly one definition under `src/rebar`; checked by
  `grep -rln 'too many tokens' src/rebar` returning exactly `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, and by the
  new guard test.
- [ ] `sizing.is_context_limit_error` still exists as a `def` in `plan_review/sizing.py` and reads
  the owner's tuple; checked by
  `grep -c 'def is_context_limit_error' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning `1` and
  `grep -n '_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning a hit.
- [ ] The three legitimate namesakes survive; checked by `grep -rln 'token limit' src/rebar`
  returning exactly `llm/failure.py` and `llm/run_failure.py`, and by
  `grep -c 'context_length_exceeded' src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` returning `3`.
- [ ] `completion_failures.py::_is_token_exhaustion` is unchanged; checked by
  `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` being empty.
- [ ] No exit-code or message behaviour changes; checked by `git diff origin/main` over
  `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` and `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` being empty.
- [ ] The guard FAILS when a second copy is introduced, not merely passes clean; checked by the
  guard test's own negative case.
- [ ] The five pinning suites named in Testing pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest`
  over them and by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` showing only additions.
- [ ] Net non-test line count is negative (the epic's consolidation guarantee); checked by
  `git show --numstat` on this story's commit, excluding tests.
